question_text: Give an account of the secretions of pituitary gland.

mark_split.label: FSH, LH and the posterior lobe

verification.note: Sourced from 'My Baby Bullet-Q — Senior Inter Zoology' (Star-Q Pass Track Series, Sri Publishers, 2022), book p.35, SAQ 27. The printed exam years are the book's claim, reproduced here as appearances. Zoology-II holds only ONE source book in the corpus, so the two-book union check is structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. steps.label: The three parts
steps.why: It is called the master gland because four of its hormones — TSH, ACTH, FSH and LH — control other endocrine glands, while the rest act on the body directly.
common_mistakes: Listing the lobes but giving no hormone for the pars intermedia. It secretes MSH.
Leaving out the phrase master gland.
steps.memory_tip: Anterior, pars intermedia, posterior — front, middle, back.
steps.margin_note: Name the three parts before listing hormones.

steps.label: GH and LTH
steps.why: Growth hormone works through the liver rather than on bone directly, which is why the liver factors are named with it.
common_mistakes: Writing that GH acts only on bone. It also drives protein synthesis and cell division.
steps.memory_tip: GH grows the body; LTH runs the milk.
steps.margin_note: The anterior lobe makes six hormones. Take them two at a time.

steps.label: TSH and ACTH
steps.why: Both are orders to another gland, which is the clearest evidence that the pituitary is the master gland.
common_mistakes: Saying TSH makes thyroxine itself. It makes the thyroid make it.
Sending ACTH to the adrenal medulla. It acts on the cortex.
steps.memory_tip: TSH points at the thyroid, ACTH at the adrenal cortex.

steps.label: FSH, LH and the posterior lobe
steps.why: The same two hormones act on the ovary in a woman and the testis in a man, which is why each has two named jobs.
common_mistakes: Giving FSH and LH only a female role. Both act in males too.
steps.memory_tip: FSH grows the follicle; LH releases the egg. Oxytocin pushes out, vasopressin holds water in.
steps.margin_note: Close with the posterior lobe. Two hormones, two functions.

LH makes Leydig cells produce testosterone
